content.user_title: Publish Files and Static Sites to Brewpage
content.value_statement: Sharing a document or static demo often requires a separate hosting workflow. This skill uploads selected content to brewpage.app and returns a shareable link.
actual_capabilities: Route text and Markdown to rendered pages, inline JSON to JSON hosting, and local files to file uploads.
Package built static directories into ZIP archives while preserving relative asset paths and selecting an entry page.
Inspect supplied ZIP archives with size budgets and integrity checks before uploading a private snapshot.
Require digest-bound confirmation for archives containing unexpected or sensitive filenames.
Support namespace, expiration, password-file, and delivery-mode choices for publication.
Save returned owner tokens and publication metadata in mode 600 local history with verified Git exclusion inside repositories.
limitations: Requires macOS, Linux, or WSL with Bash, curl, jq, and Python; Git is required in repositories, and sites need additional tools.
Hosts built static content, not application servers; sites need an HTML entry and must satisfy service limits.
Checks archive filenames, not embedded secrets; unlisted links remain accessible to anyone with the link unless password protection is enabled.
Requires access to brewpage.app and does not provide permanent hosting; requested retention defaults to 15 days and remains server-controlled.

use_cases.title: Share a Review Document
use_cases.description: Publish a selected report or Markdown document and return a link for reviewers after confirming visibility and password choices.

use_cases.title: Publish a Static Demo
use_cases.description: Upload a built demo directory with its assets, inspect the manifest, and share the returned site link.

use_cases.title: Share a Temporary Data Sample
use_cases.description: Publish a sanitized inline JSON sample with a short requested expiration for a debugging discussion.

prompt_templates.title: Publish a Short Note
prompt_templates.prompt: Publish this note to brewpage.app: [note]. Ask me to choose the namespace and password protection before uploading.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: share text as a rendered page.

prompt_templates.title: Share a Local File
prompt_templates.prompt: Publish [file path] for one day. Show its size and type, then ask for my namespace and password choices.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: upload one selected file with a short requested lifetime.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy Built Site Output
prompt_templates.prompt: Publish the built site at [directory] with [entry file]. Show the archive manifest and ask for namespace and password choices before upload.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: publish a static site with relative assets and an explicit entry.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Supplied Archive
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect [ZIP path] for publication with [password file path]. Ask for my namespace choice and approval of any flagged manifest and exact review digest.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review unexpected archive entries before authorizing their upload.

output_examples.input: Publish a reviewed project report using an unlisted namespace and no password.
output: Owner token saved in protected local history.
The link is unlisted, but anyone with it can open the report.

output_examples.input: Publish a built static site with a selected HTML entry.
output: Published site: [exact link returned by brewpage.app]
Owner token saved in protected local history.

output_examples.input: Publish an archive containing a filename marked as sensitive.
output: Review the archive manifest, flagged entries, and SHA256 digest.
Approval applies only to the reviewed archive bytes.

best_practices: Publish only reviewed build output and remove embedded secrets before approving any archive.
Confirm namespace and password choices explicitly; use a password file when link possession alone is insufficient protection.
Keep owner-token history private and use the exact returned URL, metadata, and expiration when managing publications.
anti_patterns: Treating an unlisted namespace as authentication or publishing confidential content without appropriate authorization.
Uploading a source repository or approving sensitive archive entries without reviewing the actual contents.
Printing passwords or owner tokens in chat, or assuming an update renews the publication expiration.

faq.question: What can I publish?
faq.answer: You can publish text, Markdown, inline JSON, individual files, built static directories, or supplied ZIP archives.

faq.question: Do I need a Brewpage account?
faq.answer: The documented publishing workflow requires no account. Optional account features are separate from local publishing.

faq.question: Is an unlisted namespace private?
faq.answer: It is not listed or indexed, but anyone with its link can open it. Choose password protection when you need access restrictions.

faq.question: How are passwords and owner tokens handled?
faq.answer: Passwords come from selected local files through private header files. Owner tokens are saved in protected local history, not printed in chat.

faq.question: Does archive inspection detect every secret?
faq.answer: No. It filters or flags filenames and checks archive integrity and budgets. It does not scan file contents for embedded secrets.

faq.question: How long do publications remain available?
faq.answer: The requested default is 15 days. Server expiration metadata is authoritative, and content updates do not automatically renew retention.
